target_customer: Enterprise marketing and events teams buying a premium virtual event and webinar platform on annual contracts
problem: Existing webinar tools focused on registration and analytics rather than a polished live experience.
business_model: B2B SaaS annual contracts in the five figure range (TechCrunch, Nov 2020)

founders.name: Roberto Ortiz
founders.background_notes: YC page says designer turned CEO.

founders.name: John Keh
founders.role: Founder and CEO per YC company page
founders.background_notes: Listed only on the YC company page; not named in press found.

founders.name: Jerry Shen
founders.background_notes: Sole founder on the YC launch post; press calls him a co-founder with his brother.

founders.name: Tiger Shen
founders.background_notes: Brother of Jerry Shen per Local News Matters.

competitors.name: ON24
competitors.what: Webinar platform focused on registration and analytics

technical_complexity.rationale: Live broadcast studio, custom branding and networking at event scale, built quickly after a pandemic pivot.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded rivals and Zoom could add features; premium design was the main edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Hopin raised $125M by Nov 2020 per TechCrunch; the virtual events category later collapsed (Hopin sold its events product to RingCentral in 2023).

market_need_then: COVID-19 moved events online in 2020 and investors rushed into virtual events (Skift, Oct 2020).

branding.domain_note: experiencewelcome.com, a prefix domain because welcome.com was not theirs.

identity.voice_and_tone: Premium, enterprise, Apple Keynote style per YC page

branding.brand_signature: Positioning as the Ritz-Carlton of virtual events

brand_strength.rationale: The premium Ritz-Carlton pitch got press at the Series A, but the name Welcome is generic and the domain is a prefix variant.

pivots.why: Pandemic pushed events online (Local News Matters, as relayed by search)

outcome_analysis: Welcome pivoted from restaurant software to virtual events just after YC and raised a $12 million Series A led by Kleiner Perkins in November 2020 at the peak of the virtual events boom. YC lists it inactive and a competitor blog says users report a shutdown, but the cause is not confirmed by Welcome or neutral press, so no failure factor is assigned. The wider category collapsed after 2021 as in person events returned.
notes: Series A stated by TechCrunch, Kleiner Perkins and Pilot page; VCBacked lists June 2022, treated as an error. Total raised not found, so earlier or later rounds may be missing. Shutdown rests on a competitor blog (Univid) plus YC inactive; experiencewelcome.com returned 503. John Keh appears only on the YC company page; the launch post lists only Jerry Shen. Competitors are from the undated YC launch post. Education and prior employers not found.
